lectures.title: Introduction — What Are Agentic Systems?
lectures.description: Course logistics, a brief history of agents, and the anatomy of an agent: LLM core, reasoning, memory, tools, and environment. Compound AI systems and workflows vs. agents, plus the key challenges of reliability, training, safety, and evaluation.

readings.text: Zaharia et al. "The Shift from Models to Compound AI Systems." BAIR Blog (2024).
Weng. "LLM Powered Autonomous Agents." Lil'Log (2023).
Kapoor et al. "AI Agents That Matter." TMLR (2025).

lectures.title: LLMs for Builders
lectures.description: Language model internals for agent builders: decoding strategies, transformer attention (including linear and hybrid) and context length, the pretraining-to-post-training pipeline, inference and test-time scaling, structured I/O and constrained decoding, and context engineering.

readings.text: Vaswani et al. "Attention Is All You Need." NeurIPS (2017).
Katharopoulos et al. "Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention." ICML (2020).
Rajasekaran et al. "Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents." Anthropic (2025).

lectures.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
lectures.description: Why retrieval helps, then the RAG pipeline end to end: indexing (chunking, contextual retrieval, RAPTOR, HNSW), retrievers from BM25 and DPR to hybrid search, reranking, and ColBERT, agentic RAG (Self-RAG, Search-R1), and common failure modes. Plus a course project overview.

readings.text: Lewis et al. "Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks." NeurIPS (2020).
Karpukhin et al. "Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering." EMNLP (2020).
Khattab & Zaharia. "ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT." SIGIR (2020).

lectures.title: Tool Use & Function Calling
lectures.description: Why LLMs need tools and how they learn to use them: Toolformer, scaling to thousands of APIs with Gorilla and ToolLLM, standard interfaces from REST to function calling to MCP, evaluating tool use with BFCL, ToolBench, and τ-bench, and common failure modes.

readings.text: Schick et al. "Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools." NeurIPS (2023).
Patil et al. "Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs." NeurIPS (2024).
Model Context Protocol Specification, revision 2025-06-18. modelcontextprotocol.io (2025).

lectures.title: Frameworks & Orchestration
lectures.description: The data, system, and evals pillars of agent engineering, with live demos of DSPy (signatures, modules, optimizers) and LangGraph (state, nodes, edges). A tour of open-source agent harnesses (mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, Pi), durable orchestration with Temporal, observability tooling, and best practices.

readings.text: Khattab et al. "DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines." ICLR (2024).
LangChain. "LangGraph Overview." LangChain Docs.
Arena.ai. "HarnessTax: How Much Does the Harness Matter for Coding Agents?" Arena Blog (2026).

lectures.title: Agent Design Patterns & Scaffolds
lectures.description: Workflows vs. agents and the design patterns for each: five composable workflow patterns, reasoning and acting patterns (ReAct, Reflexion, CodeAct, ReWOO), and context-management patterns (event logs, compaction, observation masking, context isolation). Case study of the Pi harness.

readings.text: Yao et al. "ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models." ICLR (2023).
Schluntz & Zhang. "Building Effective AI Agents." Anthropic (2024).
LangChain. "Context Engineering." LangChain Blog (2025).

additional.text: Shinn et al. "Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning." NeurIPS (2023).
Wang et al. "Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents." ICML (2024).

lectures.title: Agent Memory Architectures
lectures.description: Why agents need memory and the four types (working, episodic, semantic, procedural). Four architecture patterns: skill libraries, tiered hierarchies like MemGPT, reflective consolidation, and memory maintenance. Memory benchmarks and open problems in forgetting, privacy, and over-personalization.

readings.text: Sumers et al. "Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents." TMLR (2024).
Packer et al. "MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems." arXiv (2023).
Park et al. "Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior." UIST (2023).

lectures.title: Multi-Agent Systems
lectures.description: When to use single vs. multi-agent systems and how to build them: orchestration patterns (orchestrator, swarm, hybrid), communication through handoffs, message boards, and the A2A protocol, and coordination infrastructure (task ledgers, shared memory, worktree isolation). Why multi-agent systems fail.

readings.text: Wu et al. "AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation." COLM (2024).
Cemri et al. "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?" NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks (2025).
Kim et al. "Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems." arXiv (2025).

lectures.title: Optimization
lectures.description: When optimization pays off and how to do it: context optimization (bootstrapped few-shot, MIPROv2, OPRO, TextGrad, GEPA), weight optimization (SFT on agent rollouts, RL with PPO and GRPO, on-policy distillation), agents as optimizers (Darwin Gödel Machine, autoresearch), and when to optimize prompts vs. weights.

readings.text: Agrawal et al. "GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning." ICLR (2026).
Opsahl-Ong et al. "Optimizing Instructions and Demonstrations for Multi-Stage Language Model Programs." EMNLP (2024).
Shao et al. "DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models." arXiv (2024).

lectures.title: 📺 Guest Lecture: Terminal-Bench
lectures.description: Ryan Marten and Alex Shaw (Laude Institute), co-creators of Terminal-Bench, on benchmarking how well AI agents accomplish real-world tasks in a terminal environment.

readings.text: Terminal-Bench project site (leaderboard, tasks, and harness).
Merrill et al. "Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces." ICLR (2026).

lectures.title: What Data Do Agents Need?
lectures.description: Traces, demonstrations, and feedback, data for optimization vs. evaluation, data flywheels, synthetic data generation, and collecting data from human-agent interaction.

readings.text: Shankar. "Data Flywheels for LLM Applications." (2024).

additional.text: Tan et al. "Large Language Models for Data Annotation and Synthesis: A Survey." EMNLP (2024).

lectures.title: Data Selection & Quality
lectures.description: Finding maximally informative data, filtering and selection strategies, tiny-but-targeted benchmarks, annotation practices, quality assessment, and building datasets from agent traces.

readings.text: Yang et al. "SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents." NeurIPS D&B (2025).
Shankar et al. "Who Validates the Validators? Aligning LLM-Assisted Evaluation with Human Preferences." UIST (2024).

additional.text: Zhou et al. "LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment." NeurIPS (2023).

lectures.title: Evaluation Fundamentals & Benchmark Design
lectures.description: Why evals are hard, the 4-tuple framework (request, environment, stopping criteria, scorer), designing each component, properties of good benchmarks, realistic scaffolding, and reliability dimensions.

readings.text: Zhu et al. "Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks." (2025).

additional.text: Press. "How to Build Good Language Modeling Benchmarks." (2024).
Polo et al. "tinyBenchmarks: Evaluating LLMs with Fewer Examples." ICML (2024).

lectures.title: LLM-as-Judge & Evaluation Infrastructure
lectures.description: The three grader types, designing judge prompts, known biases, pairwise vs. pointwise evaluation, non-determinism metrics (pass@k vs. pass^k), harness design, and Anthropic's 8-step roadmap.

readings.text: Grace et al. "Demystifying Evals for AI Agents." Anthropic (2026).
Zheng et al. "Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena." NeurIPS (2023).
Ryan et al. "AutoMetrics: Approximate Human Judgements with Automatically Generated Evaluators." ICLR (2026).

additional.text: Zhu et al. "AutoLibra: Agent Metric Induction from Open-Ended Human Feedback." ICLR (2026).

lectures.title: Agent Safety & Guardrails
lectures.description: Privacy risks of tool access, prompt injection (including indirect injection), red-teaming, sandboxing and permission models, output guardrails, liability considerations, responsible deployment, and human-in-the-loop patterns.

readings.text: Shao et al. "PrivacyLens: Evaluating Privacy Norm Awareness of LMs in Action." NeurIPS D&B (2024).
Zhang & Yang. "Searching for Privacy Risks in LLM Agents via Simulation." arXiv (2025).
Li. "Agentic LLMs as Powerful Deanonymizers." arXiv (2026).

additional.text: Wen et al. "Contextualized Privacy Defense for LLM Agents." arXiv (2026).
OpenAI. "Understanding Prompt Injections: A Frontier Security Challenge." (2025).

lectures.title: Coding & Software Agents
lectures.description: How coding agents work end to end: the SWE-agent, Claude Code, and OpenHands architectures, scaffolds as design decisions, SWE-bench and the 4-tuple framework in practice, and the future of software development with agents.

readings.text: Yang et al. "SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering." NeurIPS (2024).
Wang et al. "OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers." ICLR (2025).

additional.text: Anthropic. "Claude Code: Best Practices for Agentic Coding." (2025).
Young. "Effective Harnesses for Long-Running Agents." Anthropic (2025).
Jimenez et al. "SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?" ICLR (2024).

lectures.title: Proactive Agents
lectures.description: From reactive to proactive agents: General User Models (GUM), Next Action Prediction, open-source proactive personal agents, privacy and trust implications, and when agents should initiate vs. wait (mixed initiative).

readings.text: Shaikh et al. "Creating General User Models from Computer Use." UIST (2025).

additional.text: Shaikh et al. "Learning Next Action Predictors from Human-Computer Interaction." arXiv (2026).

lectures.title: Frontiers & Open Problems
lectures.description: Multimodal agents, web agents and computer use, science agents, long-running agent architectures, production and observability (tracing, monitoring, cost management), and open problems in reliability, scalability, and interpretability.

additional.text: Xie et al. "OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real Computer Environments." NeurIPS D&B (2024).
Yao et al. "WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents." NeurIPS (2022).
